sources_cited: CIA Senior Executive Intelligence Brief, 23 March 2001
key_claims: The Taliban leadership allows Bin Ladin to stay in Afghanistan despite UN sanctions.
The Taliban need Bin Ladin's money and fighters for their civil war.
Taliban leaders cite the Pashtun tribal code of protecting guests as a reason to shelter him.
CIA analysts judge the Taliban would surrender Bin Ladin only after a victory in Afghanistan and in exchange for diplomatic recognition and reconstruction aid.
The Taliban would deny any deal to save face and avoid backlash from Afghan and Pakistani supporters and from Arabs sympathetic to Bin Ladin.
